claims.text: Conventional molten-Cu infiltration or Cu-powder mixing of W–Cu composites typically results in phase separation, incomplete wetting, and voids.
Tungsten particles will be conformally coated with an ultrathin Cu layer by vapor deposition before SPS consolidation.
Applied pressure during SPS can close interparticle voids and densify a powder compact.
Vapor-coated W particles followed by SPS will improve W–Cu interfacial bonding.
Vapor-coated W particles followed by SPS will eliminate void formation.
A continuous conformal Cu coating on W surfaces will ensure nearly perfect interfacial contact during SPS.
The pre-applied Cu layer will enhance wetting at W–Cu interfaces.
The pre-applied Cu layer will enhance interparticle diffusion during sintering.
Enhanced wetting and diffusion will minimize void formation.
Enhanced wetting and diffusion will minimize phase separation in W–Cu.
Improved W–Cu interfacial contact will produce a more uniform microstructure.
Improved interfacial contact and microstructural uniformity will enhance thermal transport.
The vapor-coated and SPS-consolidated composite will have lower void volume than composites made by conventional Cu infiltration or Cu-powder mixing.
The vapor-coated composite will have higher thermal conductivity than the conventional infiltration or powder-mixing baseline.
The vapor-coated composite will preserve or sustain mechanical durability under simulated fusion-relevant irradiation.
Keeping SPS temperatures below the melting point of W will avoid melting-related defects.
The magnitude of the thermal-conductivity improvement and the long-term irradiation stability of the Cu coating are not yet quantified.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the intervention will eliminate void formation, whereas the predicted outcome makes only the weaker claim of reduced void volume.

The named baseline is traditional Cu infiltration or powder mixing, but the design says both groups receive identical SPS processing. This makes the control no longer a straightforward conventional-infiltration baseline and leaves the actual fabrication comparison ambiguous.

The main claim requires mechanical durability to be preserved or sustained, while the falsification rule appears to require an improvement in mechanical properties; preservation and improvement are different criteria.
